issues.failure_explanation: For a linear SDE with drift matrix A, the covariance obeys dSigma = A Sigma + Sigma A^T + 2C. Here A = -(gamma/kappa)(I - (beta/kappa) P_t C^{-1}), so A^T contains C^{-1}P_t. The proof and the displayed ODE instead use Sigma_t(I - (beta/kappa)P_t C^{-1}), without the transpose. The term Sigma_t P_t C^{-1} should be Sigma_t C^{-1} P_t. The two agree only when P_t, C and Sigma_t commute. The lemma is stated for general preconditioners, including the constant K, which need not commute.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Sigma_t P_t C^{-1} by Sigma_t C^{-1} P_t (the transpose) in the proof and in the displayed ODE. The commuting-case uses stay valid.
issues.overall_effect: The covariance evolution is wrong for non-commuting preconditioners such as K. The later uses (the corollary and the CBS equivalence lemma) only treat commuting cases and are unaffected.
issues.title: Covariance ODE for Gaussian moments drops a transpose (wrong for non-commuting preconditioners)
issues.why_classification: A one-term local correction that follows from the proof's own Lyapunov structure, with no change to any result actually used downstream.

issues.failure_explanation: By the lemma's formula, at Sigma_t = Sigma the preconditioner is (alpha+1+lambda^{-1})^{-1} Sigma, not (lambda^{-1}+alpha+1) Sigma. Inserting the stated value into the condition kappa I = (gamma - beta/(beta+1)) Sigma C^{-1} would give gamma = (lambda^{-1}+alpha+1) kappa + beta/(beta+1). That contradicts the corollary's formula, which has the factor (1/lambda+alpha+1)^{-1}. The proof step is therefore wrong as written, although the stated gamma is the correct one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated preconditioner by (lambda^{-1}+alpha+1)^{-1} Sigma in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the gamma formula in case (iii) is wrong as written. The final formula is correct, and cases (i) and (ii) follow from the correct value.
issues.title: Stationary preconditioner value for case (iii) inverted in the proof
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic correction fixed by the lemma's own formula; the statement and the method are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses gamma = 2 alpha'/(alpha'+1), but gamma is not among the stated parameter choices. Also, lambda = alpha'/(alpha-alpha') is only positive, as required by the definition of the weighted preconditioner, when alpha > alpha'. It is negative for alpha < alpha' and undefined for alpha = alpha'. The hypothesis 'alpha > 0' does not guarantee a valid lambda.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add gamma = 2 alpha'/(alpha'+1) to the parameter list. Restrict to alpha > alpha' (or allow lambda = infinity when alpha = alpha').
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the lemma holds for an unspecified gamma and covers parameter values where lambda is invalid. The conclusion m_t = m'_{ct}, Sigma_t = Sigma'_{ct} is only justified for the specific gamma and alpha > alpha'.
issues.title: Equivalence lemma omits gamma and allows lambda<=0 or undefined
issues.why_classification: Adding the omitted parameter and the sign condition fixes the statement; the proof is otherwise unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: With kappa = alpha, beta = alpha', one gets P_t = (2(alpha' Sigma^{-1} + Sigma_t^{-1}))^{-1} and C^{-1} = (alpha/alpha')(alpha' Sigma^{-1} + Sigma_t^{-1}). Hence P_t C^{-1} = (alpha/(2 alpha')) I, not (alpha/alpha') I. As written, the second line gives -2c Sigma_t + 2c Sigma_t = 0, so dSigma = 2C. That does not match the next line, 2[C - c Sigma_t]. The step does not follow from the displayed expression.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (alpha/(2 alpha')) I in the second line.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed intermediate step is incorrect; the next line is reached only after correcting the factor 1/2.
issues.title: Factor-2 inconsistency in the covariance computation of the equivalence proof
issues.why_classification: A local arithmetic fix; the subsequent lines and the conclusion are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The preceding line, 2[c(Sigma_t - alpha' Sigma_t(...)^{-1}(Sigma_t - Sigma)) - c Sigma_t], simplifies to -2c alpha' Sigma_t (Sigma+alpha' Sigma_t)^{-1}(Sigma_t - Sigma). The last line drops the minus sign. As written it is the time-reversed (unstable) ODE, not 'the same ODE as (dot-Sigma') accelerated by c'. The deduction Sigma_t = Sigma'_{ct} therefore does not follow from the displayed final line.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the minus sign in the final line.
issues.overall_effect: The concluding equality of covariance ODEs is false as written. It is true after restoring the sign, so the lemma's conclusion survives.
issues.title: Sign error: derived covariance ODE does not match the CBS ODE it is said to equal
issues.why_classification: A single sign slip, with the correct sign forced by the preceding line; no change to the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the case where $G$ is linear, \cref{eq:compare:laldi:aldi} is equivalent to \cref{eq:ips:lang:lang-int} and, hence, has $\pi$ as an invariant distribution

issues.failure_explanation: With V = (1/2)||y-G(u)||^2_Gamma + (1/2)||u-u0||^2_{Gamma0}, the drift C grad log pi-hat contains -C Gamma0^{-1}(u-u0). Equation (aldi) has a plus sign, making the prior term repulsive. The localized version a few lines later uses the correct minus sign. With the plus sign, the equation is not equivalent to the interacting Langevin dynamics for linear G, and pi is not invariant. The accompanying claim is therefore false for the equation as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change + to - in front of the prior term in (aldi).
issues.overall_effect: The stated gradient-free ALDI dynamics, and the claimed equivalence to the interacting Langevin dynamics for linear G, are incorrect as written.
issues.title: Wrong sign of the prior term in the ALDI/EKS dynamics
issues.why_classification: A one-sign fix forced by the derivation and by the localized formula; no result of the paper depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this paper we always choose $\alpha=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimator is labelled as the particle version of mu_{beta, kappa C/beta}, whose weights are w_{beta, kappa C/beta}(v;u) = exp(-||v-u||^2_{kappa C/beta}/2) pi-hat(v)^beta. The weights actually used are w_{alpha, lambda C}, which are the preconditioner weights with a different power and a different distance scale. With the paper's defaults (alpha = 0, lambda = infinity for the unweighted preconditioner), these weights are all 1. The drift would then target the plain ensemble mean, ignoring pi-hat, beta and kappa. The algorithm (comput:lcbs-alg) as defined is not the localized CBS drift.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace w_{alpha,lambda C}^{ij} by w_{beta, kappa C/beta}^{ij} in both numerator and denominator (recomputing the weights with the preconditioner of particle i).
issues.overall_effect: The particle drift in the localized CBS algorithm is mis-specified as written. Its guarantees and the interpretation of the numerical experiments depend on the intended weights.
issues.title: Random-batch weighted mean uses the wrong weights (alpha, lambda instead of beta, kappa/beta)
issues.why_classification: A local substitution of the correct weight function, which is clear from the estimator's own subscripts; the method is unchanged.
